ONLINE CATALOG Interdisciplinary Neuroscience Program Faculty Overview The B.S. program is designed to provide studentsyou with a foundational understanding of the brain and the nervous system. Our interdisciplinary approach will provide studentsyou with knowledge in areas such as nervous system diseases and current therapeutic strategies, the cellular molecular biology of the nervous system, cognition and behavior. Students will You’ll have the opportunity to gain experience with a variety multitude of experimental approaches and techniques used to solve unanswered questions in the field of neuroscience. Three There are three major options are currently available for the B.S. degree: • a major in Clinical Neuroscience from the College of Health Sciences, • a major in Molecular Neuroscience from the College of Environment and Life Sciences, and • a major in Neuropharmacology from the College of Pharmacy. The INP option for different majors is unique and makes URI truly distinct when it comes to undergraduate neuroscience education. The interdisciplinary nature of the program allows students you access to a broad range of faculty with expertise in neuroscience research labs across the campus as well asand the George and Anne Ryan Institute for Neuroscience. Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages) Background: This proposal is requesting the addition of tracks to an existing degree program, the MS in Dietetics. 2 credentialing requirement which states that all students need a master’s degree with experiential learning to become Registered Dietitian Nutritionists (RDNs).
